findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There were various cooked food that lacked date marking inside of the prep cooler. These items were cooked noodles and cooked chicken. Discussed with the PIC and the items were date marked to correct the violation. Ensure that time/temperature control (TCS) foods are date marked with the date of preparation if being held for longer than 24 hours in house.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The baffles of the ventilation system were observed heavily accumulated with dried grease. The PIC mentioned that the facility cleans the baffles every Saturday, however, the baffles were black in color and will need to be cleaned more frequently due to the amount of frying in the facility. The ansul system was also accumulated in grease debris. See that a professional hood cleaning company services the duct work of the hood system.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
findings.comment: There isn’t any hot water available at the handwashing sink inside of the only functional bathroom. The PIC mentioned that the facility is aware of the issue and a plumber will be to service the sink soon. Ensure that all handsinks are equipped with hot water to be sure that hands are getting washed properly. Will follow-up on 6/22/2026 to check for running hot water.
findings.citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: There is massive leak at the handwashing sink across from the cookline. Waste water is spilling onto the floor from the pipe underneath the basin. The facility is aware of the leak and will have a plumber service the sink soon. Ensure that all piping of handsinks are in good repair and never in leaking condition. Will follow-up on 6/22/2026.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Overall, the facility could benefit from a detail cleaning. Floors and walls throughout the kitchen are coated with dried grease and debris. During slow periods, be sure to pull equipment from wall to sweep, mop, and scrub accumulated areas. The inner surfaces inside of the drawer cooler were observed with spilled liquids and debris. Shown it the PIC. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as frequent as possible to keep them clean.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces require cleaning:

(1) THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: The dust and other soil residue accumulation on the walk-in cooler fans.

(2) The accumulation of debris on the shelves above the triple sink.

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there is a missing electrical outlet cover to the left of the front hand washing sink. Ensure that the missing outlet is replaced or the hole in the wall sealed to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the soda machine nozzles had an accumulation of debris when the inspector arrived at the facility. The PIC removed the soda nozzles and washed, rinsed, and sanitized them during the inspection. The inspector educated that the nozzles must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris. Ensure that the soda machine nozzles are always clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the following non-food contact surfaces needed to be cleaned: (1) The accumulation of food debris on the bottom shelf of the freezer; and (2) The dust and other soil residue accumulation on the fans of the walk-in cooler. The bottom shelf of the freezer and the walk-in cooler fans were cleaned to sight and touch during the inspection. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed single-use knives by the self-service soda machine stored with the handles and food contact surfaces intermixed. The PIC was educated on storing single-use utensils with the handles facing out to avoid customers contaminating food contact surfaces. Ensure that the single-use knives are stored correctly by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. Observed single use-articles stored in boxes on the floor in the back storage area. A portion of the shelving is broken which is causing the single use-articles to be stored on the ground. The PIC stated they have the parts and the shelving should be repaired soon. Ensure that all single-use articles are stored at least 6 inches above the floor to protect against contamination. 

4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Observed the front hand washing sink has a gap between the sink and the wall. The present caulking is in good condition but it is not sufficient. The facility can caulk over the present caulk to fill in the gap to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure the caulking is replaced or repaired by the next routine inspection.
